headline: No shared execution or data channels are exposed; the pair is low-risk overall, with only minor prompt-injection and compliance concerns from docs-only uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A has no exposed I/O surfaces and Agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, or MCP use. With no shared communication channel documented, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between ai-engineering-hub and python-cheatsheet.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared clipboard, file drop, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF Agent A is wrapped to emit raw instructions into a channel Agent B parses, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or file bridges.
Run both in separate sessions with no shared workspace.
Disable any future MCP connector between them unless provenance filtering is added.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, and Agent B cannot read files or use clipboard/stdin/stdout by default. Agent A also has network egress set to none, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other or outward.
conditions: IF either agent is given a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF Agent B is reconfigured to read files or accept stdin, the current conclusion no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave Agent B file-read and stdin/stdout surfaces disabled.
Confirm Agent A remains network-isolated before use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A is documented as non-runnable and Agent B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable capability to conflict over, so the pair cannot contend for shared writes in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF Agent B gains write access to a shared directory, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF Agent A becomes runnable with write or git permissions, reassess for overlap.
mitigations: Do not grant Agent A runtime permissions without a lock/coordination layer.
Avoid placing both agents on the same mutable repository.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is a documentation-only content writer and Agent A is an unverified open-source hub; there is no evidence that B automatically treats A's outputs as authoritative. Any cascade would require an external orchestrator to feed A's material into B, so the pathway is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an orchestrator pipes Agent A outputs directly into Agent B drafts without review, cascading error risk increases.
IF Agent B is tasked to publish or act on A-generated claims, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before publication.
Require citations or source links for any A-derived claim.
Keep Agent B in drafting-only mode for A-generated content.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or sensitive data handling mismatch is documented. Agent A touches no data classes and Agent B lists no secrets, so there is no compliance pathway evidenced in the profiles; the other agent is not separately cited because no cross-border or regulated-data flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance must be rechecked.
IF a jurisdictional or retention policy is added later, the current assessment may no longer apply.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Document retention and residency settings before deployment.
Keep both agents on non-sensitive content only.
